name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
bestUsedFor: Most defensible routine psychiatric uses are depression, anxiety-spectrum distress, and broader transdiagnostic emotional disorders when avoidance and fusion are prominent.

name: Adherence-Focused Brief Work / Adherence Therapy
bestUsedFor: Most defensible and specific use is in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders and other long-term psychiatric illnesses where medication non-adherence is clearly driving relapse, symptom persistence, or repeated admission.

name: Adolescent CBT
bestUsedFor: Best-supported for adolescent depression and anxiety presentations where CBT mechanisms fit.

name: Adolescent-focused psychotherapy for anorexia nervosa
bestUsedFor: Best for children and young people with anorexia nervosa when FT-AN is unacceptable, contraindicated, or ineffective.

name: Advocacy-informed therapeutic work
bestUsedFor: Best in community psychiatry, rehabilitation, severe mental illness, complex psychosocial presentations, and recovery-oriented care where progress depends on both treatment and access to practical supports.

name: App-supported therapy
bestUsedFor: Best as an adjunct to therapy or as part of structured low-intensity guided digital CBT.

name: Applied Relaxation / Relaxation-Based Therapy
bestUsedFor: Strongest formal guideline support is for generalised anxiety disorder, where NICE includes applied relaxation as a high-intensity psychological treatment option alongside CBT.

name: Arts Therapies for Psychosis
bestUsedFor: NICE says to consider offering arts therapies to all people with psychosis or schizophrenia, particularly for the alleviation of negative symptoms.

name: Behaviour Therapy
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is when the main maintaining factor is behavioural rather than primarily interpersonal or insight-based.

name: Behavioural Activation (BA)
bestUsedFor: Strongly indicated for depression, especially when inactivity, withdrawal, reduced routine, and loss of reinforcement are prominent.

name: Behavioural Couples Therapy (BCT)
bestUsedFor: Strongest psychiatric guideline use is depression when relationship problems may be contributing to the depression or involving the partner may help treatment.

name: Behavioural Couples Therapy for Substance Use Disorders (BCT-SUD)
bestUsedFor: Best used when the patient is in a committed relationship and the partner is willing to participate.

name: Behavioural parent training
bestUsedFor: Best for oppositional defiant disorder, conduct disorder, disruptive behaviour, and children at high risk of conduct disorder.

name: Brief low-intensity CBT
bestUsedFor: Best as an early-intervention or stepped-care treatment for mild or emerging common mental health problems.

name: Brief supportive psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best as a pragmatic short-term intervention in inpatient psychiatry, CL psychiatry, ED/crisis recovery, early engagement, post-discharge follow-up, adjustment to diagnosis, medical illness, grief/stress reactions, and bridging while waiting for more specific therapy.

name: Bright-light therapy
bestUsedFor: Best as an adjunctive treatment for depressive disorders when a low-burden somatic option is attractive, especially where circadian disruption or preference for non-drug augmentation is relevant.

name: Carer groups
bestUsedFor: Strongest guideline-backed use is in psychosis and schizophrenia, where carer-focused education and support programmes are explicitly recommended.

name: Carer Interventions
bestUsedFor: Best established in psychosis / schizophrenia, where NICE states that carers of adults with psychosis or schizophrenia should be offered carer-focused education and support programmes, and parents/carers of newly diagnosed children and young people with bipolar disorder, psychosis, or schizophrenia should be given information about carer-focused education and support.

name: Carer-Focused Education and Support / Carer Psychoeducation in Psychosis
bestUsedFor: Best supported for carers of adults with psychosis or schizophrenia.

name: Carer-supported meal-based interventions
bestUsedFor: Strongest in young people with anorexia nervosa or restrictive eating disorders, especially where family/carer support can be mobilised.

name: CBT-informed psychological intervention for self-harm
bestUsedFor: Best for adults who self-harm and are receiving continuing support after an episode or repeated episodes.

name: Child CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for child anxiety disorders and selected depressive presentations when adapted to age and formulation.

name: Circadian / rhythm-based interventions
bestUsedFor: Best-supported psychiatric uses are 2 main groups.

name: Client-Directed / Feedback-Informed Brief Work
bestUsedFor: Most useful as an adjunct across many therapies rather than a stand-alone primary treatment.

name: Cognitive Analytic Therapy (CAT)
bestUsedFor: Most defensible use is personality disorder and other complex, chronic presentations where repeated maladaptive relational patterns are central.

name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)
bestUsedFor: Strongest broad evidence-backed uses are depression and anxiety disorders.

name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Bipolar Depression / Bipolar Relapse Prevention
bestUsedFor: Best used as an adjunctive psychotherapy in bipolar disorder, especially for bipolar depression, residual symptoms, and relapse prevention in people who are not acutely manic.

name: Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia
bestUsedFor: Best first-line psychological treatment for chronic insomnia, including insomnia with comorbid mental or physical health problems.

name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I)
bestUsedFor: Best used for chronic insomnia disorder in adults of any age, including people with comorbid conditions.

name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Psychosis (CBTp)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for psychosis and schizophrenia, including people at increased risk of psychosis, first and subsequent acute episodes, and the recovery phase when positive or negative symptoms continue to affect distress or function.

name: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT)
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is PTSD.

name: Cognitive Remediation Therapy (CRT)
bestUsedFor: Best supported in rehabilitation for adults with complex psychosis, particularly when cognitive impairment is contributing to poor everyday function, educational difficulty, or problems engaging in vocational recovery.

name: Cognitive stimulation therapy
bestUsedFor: Best for mild to moderate dementia.

name: Cognitive Therapy
bestUsedFor: Classic strongest uses are depression and anxiety disorders, especially where maladaptive appraisals, rumination, or catastrophic thinking are central.

name: Cognitive Therapy for PTSD (CT-PTSD)
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is PTSD in adults.

name: Community Reinforcement and Family Training (CRAFT)
bestUsedFor: Best used when the person with substance use disorder is refusing or avoiding treatment, but a partner, parent, or other close support person is seeking help.

name: Community reinforcement approach
bestUsedFor: Best for alcohol and other drug use disorders where lifestyle, reinforcement, social context, and recovery capital are central.

name: Community-based psychosocial intervention
bestUsedFor: Best in severe mental illness, complex psychosis, long-term community care, step-down pathways, and cases where repeated acute treatment has not translated into stable community functioning.

name: Compassion-focused therapy
bestUsedFor: Best when shame and self-criticism are prominent, including some depression, eating-disorder, trauma-related, and transdiagnostic distress presentations.

name: Constructivist therapies
bestUsedFor: Best for identity, grief, adjustment, self-meaning, and broader distress where a meaning-construction model fits better than a symptom-protocol model.

name: Contingency Management (CM)
bestUsedFor: Best used for stimulant use disorder, for illicit drug use in methadone maintenance, and for engagement / abstinence targets in drug services.

name: Coping-Skills Interventions
bestUsedFor: Best used as a low-intensity or adjunctive intervention for common mental health problems, subthreshold or mixed distress states, adjustment-related difficulty, stress-related functional decline, and as a bridge while waiting for or building toward more specific treatment.

name: Couples Therapy
bestUsedFor: The clearest current psychiatric guideline-backed use is behavioural couples therapy for depression when relationship problems may be contributing to depression, or when involving the partner may help treatment.

name: Craving-management interventions
bestUsedFor: Best for alcohol, cannabis, stimulant, opioid, sedative, and polysubstance use where craving is a clear relapse driver.

name: Crisis intervention / crisis-oriented brief therapy
bestUsedFor: Best for acute crisis presentations where the person needs immediate containment and a short practical intervention.

name: Cue Exposure Therapy (CET) for Substance Use Disorders
bestUsedFor: Best viewed as a selective or emerging adjunctive treatment, not a default first-line SUD psychotherapy.

name: DBT skills groups
bestUsedFor: Strongest psychiatric use is within a comprehensive DBT programme for borderline personality disorder or closely related chronic emotion-dysregulation presentations, especially where recurrent self-harm or severe affective instability is a major treatment target.

name: DBT-Informed Adjunctive Emotion-Regulation Work for Eating Disorders
bestUsedFor: Most defensible for bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, and some complex eating-disorder presentations where emotion dysregulation is clearly central.

name: Developmental social-skills interventions
bestUsedFor: Best for autistic children/young people and other developmental presentations where social communication is a clear functional target.

name: Developmentally adapted DBT
bestUsedFor: Best for adolescents with recurrent self-harm, suicidal ideation, severe emotion dysregulation, emerging borderline traits, or repeated crisis presentations where a structured skills-plus-risk model is needed.

name: Developmentally adapted ERP
bestUsedFor: Best for paediatric OCD and BDD.

name: Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for borderline personality disorder / borderline personality symptoms, especially when recurrent self-harm is a major treatment priority.

name: Dignity therapy
bestUsedFor: Best in palliative care, psycho-oncology, advanced illness, neurodegenerative disease, and CL psychiatry where existential distress, dignity, meaning, and legacy are central.

name: Dyadic Therapy
bestUsedFor: The strongest and clearest uses are parent–infant / mother–infant work, especially when maternal mental health and the infant relationship are both clinically relevant.

name: Dynamic interpersonal therapy
bestUsedFor: Best-supported use is major depressive disorder, especially when interpersonal patterns, attachment insecurity, relationship loss, or relational conflict are central.

name: Eating-Disorder-Focused Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT-ED / CBT-E)
bestUsedFor: Strongest current guideline-backed use is in adults with bulimia nervosa, adults with binge eating disorder, and as one of the main options for adults with anorexia nervosa.

name: Eating-Disorder-Focused Focal Psychodynamic Therapy (FPT) for Adult Anorexia Nervosa
bestUsedFor: Best used in adults with anorexia nervosa when one of the three main adult psychotherapies already recommended by NICE — CBT-ED, MANTRA, or SSCM — has been unacceptable, contraindicated, or ineffective.

name: ECT
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is severe depressive disorder, especially where rapid response is needed, previous ECT response has been good, or other treatments have not provided adequate benefit.

name: Emotion-focused therapy
bestUsedFor: Best for emotionally driven distress where maladaptive emotion processing is central, and especially for couple distress in the couples form.

name: Empowerment-focused practice
bestUsedFor: Best as a cross-cutting psychiatric practice approach in recovery-oriented care, community psychiatry, rehabilitation, trauma-informed practice, and long-term mental healthcare.

name: Existential psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best for patients whose suffering is strongly shaped by meaning, mortality, identity, or existential conflict, including some depressive, anxiety, adjustment, and serious-illness contexts.

name: Experiential therapies
bestUsedFor: Best when emotional processing difficulty is central, especially in mood, anxiety, personality, and somatic symptom presentations.

name: Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP)
bestUsedFor: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is the clearest and strongest use.

name: Exposure and Response Prevention for Tics (ERP for Tics)
bestUsedFor: Best used for Tourette syndrome and persistent motor or vocal tic disorder when tics are distressing, impairing, painful, socially disruptive, or functionally limiting.

name: Exposure therapy
bestUsedFor: Best for anxiety disorders where avoidance maintains symptoms, including specific phobia, panic/agoraphobia, social anxiety, OCD when paired with response prevention, and PTSD when delivered as trauma-focused exposure such as prolonged exposure.

name: Exposure-Based CBT / Exposure Therapy
bestUsedFor: Strongest uses are phobic disorders, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, and exposure-based elements within broader CBT.

name: Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR)
bestUsedFor: For adults with PTSD, Phoenix Australia gives EMDR a strong recommendation.

name: Family Intervention for Psychosis
bestUsedFor: Best supported for adults with psychosis or schizophrenia who live with or are in close contact with family members or carers.

name: Family problem-solving interventions
bestUsedFor: Strongest guideline-backed use is psychosis and schizophrenia, where NICE recommends family intervention for families who live with or are in close contact with the patient.

name: Family Psychoeducation for Psychosis
bestUsedFor: Most useful for schizophrenia-spectrum and other psychotic disorders when family members or carers are closely involved and need a clearer illness model, relapse plan, and coping framework.

name: Family Therapy
bestUsedFor: Best used when the family system is clearly relevant to outcome.

name: Family-Based Treatment for Adolescent Anorexia Nervosa (FT-AN)
bestUsedFor: Best used for children and young people with anorexia nervosa.

name: Family-Based Treatment for Bulimia Nervosa (FT-BN)
bestUsedFor: Best used for children and young people with bulimia nervosa.

name: Family-Focused Psychoeducation for Bipolar Disorder
bestUsedFor: Best used for relapse prevention in bipolar disorder, especially when relatives/carers are closely involved in day-to-day life or episode detection.

name: Family-Focused Therapy for Bipolar Disorder (FFT-BD)
bestUsedFor: Most defensible use is bipolar disorder as an adjunctive longer-term psychosocial treatment, especially after an acute mood episode and when family members or caregivers are closely involved.

name: Functional Family Therapy (FFT)
bestUsedFor: Most defensible use is adolescents with behaviour / antisocial problems and young people with alcohol misuse plus significant comorbidities or limited social support.

name: Gestalt therapy
bestUsedFor: Best as an experiential psychotherapy for people with depression, anxiety, interpersonal distress, self-esteem problems, or broader psychological distress when an experiential present-focused model fits the case.

name: Good psychiatric management
bestUsedFor: Best for borderline personality disorder or clinically significant borderline traits, especially in general psychiatric, community, outpatient, ED follow-up, CL, and public-sector settings where full DBT, MBT, schema therapy, or TFP is unavailable or not required.

name: Graded Exposure
bestUsedFor: Most useful for phobic avoidance, panic disorder with avoidance, social anxiety disorder, and broader anxiety presentations where the main perpetuating factor is avoidance of feared situations rather than compulsions or trauma re-experiencing.

name: Group exposure programmes
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is anxiety disorders where exposure is first-line, especially social anxiety disorder, panic disorder with agoraphobia, and specific phobias (though individual exposure is often preferred for highly specific phobias).

name: Group psychoeducation
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is as an adjunct in bipolar disorder, especially maintenance-phase care and relapse prevention.

name: Group Psychoeducation for Bipolar Disorder
bestUsedFor: Best used for maintenance / relapse prevention in bipolar disorder, especially when the patient is not in an acute episode and can engage in a structured group format.

name: Group relapse-prevention programmes
bestUsedFor: Strongest guideline support is for adults with depression at higher risk of relapse, where NICE recommends relapse-prevention interventions including group CBT or MBCT.

name: Group social-skills training
bestUsedFor: Best as a rehabilitation or developmental intervention, especially in psychosis rehabilitation, autism social-learning programmes, and functional recovery settings.

name: Guided self-help
bestUsedFor: Best as an initial low-intensity or stepped-care treatment for milder depression and anxiety presentations, especially when symptoms are not highly complex and the patient can work independently with support.

name: Guided Self-Help for Binge Eating Disorder
bestUsedFor: Best used for adults with binge eating disorder as the initial psychological treatment step.

name: Guided Self-Help for Bulimia-Nervosa
bestUsedFor: Best used for adults with bulimia nervosa as the first psychological treatment step to consider.

name: Habit reversal training / CBIT
bestUsedFor: Best-supported use is Tourette syndrome and chronic tic disorders, where CBIT is an evidence-based behavioural treatment.

name: Habit Reversal Training for Trichotillomania and Excoriation Disorder
bestUsedFor: Best used for trichotillomania (hair-pulling disorder) and excoriation disorder (skin-picking disorder) when symptoms cause distress, impairment, visible damage, infection/scarring risk, or major shame/avoidance.

name: Harm-reduction counselling
bestUsedFor: Best for patients who are not ready for abstinence, are ambivalent, have limited contact with services, or are at high risk of preventable harm.

name: Health-anxiety-focused CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for persistent health anxiety where adequate medical assessment has not found an explanatory serious disease and the main maintaining mechanism is anxiety-driven misinterpretation and reassurance-seeking.

name: Humanistic psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best for depression and broader psychological distress where an exploratory, emotionally focused, relationship-based psychotherapy is appropriate.

name: Illness-Management-and-Recovery Style Interventions (IMR-Style Interventions)
bestUsedFor: Most useful in severe mental illness, especially schizophrenia-spectrum disorders and other long-term psychotic illnesses, when the clinical task is ongoing recovery and self-management rather than acute symptom containment alone.

name: Imagery Rehearsal Therapy (IRT) for Nightmare Disorder
bestUsedFor: Best used for nightmare disorder in adults and for persistent distressing nightmares in broader psychiatric populations.

name: Imagery rescripting
bestUsedFor: Best as a targeted technique within broader therapy for PTSD/complex trauma, social anxiety disorder with negative self-imagery, nightmares, shame-based depression, and some personality/schema presentations.

name: Inference-based CBT for OCD
bestUsedFor: Best as a selective OCD treatment when ERP is refused, poorly tolerated, or the clinical formulation is dominated by obsessional doubt, poor insight, or “imagined possibility” reasoning.

name: Integrated CBT for PTSD and Substance Use Disorders
bestUsedFor: Best used for co-occurring PTSD and SUD when the patient is stable enough for structured treatment and is willing to address trauma directly.

name: Integrated dual-diagnosis psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best for psychosis plus cannabis/stimulant use, mood disorder plus alcohol/drug use, PTSD plus substance use, personality/emotion dysregulation plus substance use, and recurrent admissions where separate mental health and AOD care keeps failing.

name: Intensive Psychodynamic Psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Most defensible for complex mental disorders where there is a combination of syndromal illness and severe personality / vulnerability features, including some borderline personality disorder and treatment-resistant depression presentations.

name: Internet-delivered CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for mild to moderate common mental health problems, especially depression and anxiety, when access, distance, mobility, or wait times are barriers.

name: Interoceptive Exposure
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is panic disorder, with or without agoraphobic avoidance, especially when the patient fears bodily sensations such as dizziness, tachycardia, breathlessness, chest tightness, depersonalisation, or feeling faint.

name: Interpersonal and Social Rhythm Therapy (IPSRT)
bestUsedFor: Best used as an adjunctive psychotherapy for bipolar disorder, especially in patients whose episodes are clearly linked to sleep/routine disruption or interpersonal stress.

name: Interpersonal Psychotherapy (IPT)
bestUsedFor: Strongest routine use is depression, especially when symptoms are closely linked to bereavement, changing roles, interpersonal conflict, or isolation.

name: Life-review therapy / reminiscence therapy
bestUsedFor: Best for older adults with depression/loneliness, dementia-care settings, aged care, palliative/CL psychiatry, and patients needing meaning, identity, continuity or life-story work.

name: Low-intensity relapse-prevention programmes
bestUsedFor: Strongest guideline-backed use is recurrent depression or depression in partial/full remission where relapse risk is higher.

name: Matrix Model
bestUsedFor: Best used for stimulant use disorder, particularly methamphetamine and cocaine use in outpatient settings.

name: Maudsley Anorexia Nervosa Treatment for Adults (MANTRA)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for adults with anorexia nervosa.

name: Meaning-centred psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best-supported use is advanced cancer, serious illness, and palliative care, where RCTs and reviews suggest benefit for meaning, spiritual well-being, and existential distress.

name: Mentalisation-Based Therapy (MBT)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for borderline personality disorder and related severe personality dysfunction where attachment stress and relational misinterpretation are central.

name: Metacognitive Therapy (MCT)
bestUsedFor: The strongest current evidence is in anxiety disorders and depression.

name: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT)
bestUsedFor: Strongest guideline-backed use is relapse prevention in recurrent depression.

name: Mindfulness-Based Relapse Prevention (MBRP)
bestUsedFor: Best viewed as an adjunctive or selective relapse-prevention treatment for SUDs rather than a clearly dominant stand-alone first-line therapy.

name: Mindfulness-based stress reduction
bestUsedFor: Best as a structured mindfulness intervention for stress, depressive symptoms, and broader distress where mindfulness practice is acceptable and safe.

name: Mindfulness-based therapies not primarily CBT-anchored
bestUsedFor: Best as a structured adjunct or selected primary intervention for stress, depressive symptoms, relapse vulnerability, and transdiagnostic distress where mindfulness practice is acceptable and safe.

name: Mindfulness-Based Therapy for Insomnia (MBTI)
bestUsedFor: Best viewed as an evidence-supported option for chronic insomnia, especially when arousal, worry, and reactive struggle with sleep are prominent.

name: Mother-Infant Therapy / Mother-Infant Psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Most defensible use is perinatal / postpartum mental health, especially where maternal symptoms and the mother–infant relationship are both clinically relevant.

name: Motivational Enhancement Therapy (MET)
bestUsedFor: Highest-yield for substance use disorders, harmful alcohol or drug use, treatment engagement problems, and early behaviour-change work when ambivalence is the main barrier.

name: Motivational Interviewing
bestUsedFor: Highest-yield in substance use disorders, harmful use, medication ambivalence, health-behaviour change, early engagement, and situations where the patient is not yet ready for direct action treatment.

name: Motivational Interviewing (MI) for Substance Use Disorders
bestUsedFor: Best used at engagement, assessment, early treatment, and whenever motivation is unstable.

name: Multi-Family Interventions
bestUsedFor: Best supported in psychosis / schizophrenia, where NICE states family intervention should take account of family preference for either single-family intervention or multi-family group intervention.

name: Multidimensional family therapy
bestUsedFor: Best for adolescents with substance use plus conduct/delinquency or complex family/system involvement.

name: Multisystemic Therapy (MST)
bestUsedFor: NICE recommends offering multimodal interventions, for example MST, to children and young people aged 11 to 17 years for conduct disorder.

name: Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET)
bestUsedFor: In Australian PTSD guidelines, NET has a conditional recommendation for adults with PTSD where trauma is linked to genocide, civil conflict, torture, political detention, or displacement.

name: Narrative therapy
bestUsedFor: Best when identity, meaning, stigma, trauma-related self-story, family/community narratives, or chronic demoralisation are central.

name: Narrative-informed community work
bestUsedFor: Best in community psychiatry, psychosocial rehabilitation, trauma-informed recovery work, youth or adult community mental health, and severe mental illness where identity, belonging, and social participation are central.

name: Neurodevelopmentally adapted psychosocial interventions
bestUsedFor: Best whenever a standard psychosocial therapy is clinically indicated but the person’s neurodevelopmental profile makes usual delivery ineffective or inaccessible.

name: Panic-focused CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, especially when recurrent panic attacks, bodily-sensation fear, anticipatory anxiety, and avoidance are central.

name: Parent Management Training (PMT)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for children with clinical levels of disruptive behaviour, especially oppositional and conduct-type presentations in younger children.

name: Parent Training
bestUsedFor: Best supported for children aged 3 to 11 years who are at high risk of oppositional defiant disorder or conduct disorder, who already have oppositional defiant disorder or conduct disorder, or who are in contact with the criminal justice system because of antisocial behaviour.

name: Parent-and-Child Training
bestUsedFor: Best used for children aged 3 to 11 years at high risk of oppositional defiant disorder or conduct disorder, who already have oppositional defiant disorder or conduct disorder, or who are in contact with the criminal justice system because of antisocial behaviour when their problems are severe and complex.

name: Parent-Child Relational Therapy
bestUsedFor: Most defensible use is where the relationship itself is a central treatment target, especially in disruptive behaviour, developmental and attachment-linked difficulty, early childhood mental health, and selected trauma or caregiving contexts.

name: Parent–Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for young children with clinically significant disruptive behaviour problems.

name: Peer recovery interventions
bestUsedFor: Best as an adjunct across the SUD care continuum, especially engagement, post-detox or post-discharge transitions, ED/hospital linkage, community recovery, opioid use disorder care, relapse recovery, and treatment retention.

name: Peer Support
bestUsedFor: Most useful in psychosis rehabilitation, community recovery work, discharge transition, engagement support, group activities, and broader recovery-oriented service delivery.

name: Peer-led groups
bestUsedFor: Best as an adjunctive recovery-oriented intervention, especially where connection, empowerment, and lived-experience modelling are central.

name: Person-centred / Rogerian therapy
bestUsedFor: Best for depression or distress where psychosocial, relationship, or employment problems are contributing and the person would prefer an emotionally exploratory, non-directive therapy.

name: Phase-Oriented Trauma Therapy
bestUsedFor: Most defensible for complex trauma / complex PTSD-type presentations where there is marked instability, chronic interpersonal trauma history, and major deficits in regulation or safety.

name: Play therapy / play-based therapies
bestUsedFor: Best as a developmentally appropriate therapy or adjunct for younger children with emotional, behavioural, relational, or adjustment difficulties, especially when verbal CBT-style work is too abstract.

name: Problem Management Plus / PM+
bestUsedFor: Best for low-resource, community, humanitarian, primary-care, stepped-care, public-health, and service-bridging settings where specialist psychotherapy access is limited.

name: Problem-Solving Therapy (PST)
bestUsedFor: Most useful for less severe depression, stress-linked depression, adjustment-related difficulty, executive overload, and patients whose distress is closely tied to unresolved current-life problems.

name: Process groups
bestUsedFor: Best for patients whose difficulties are strongly interpersonal or personality-pattern based, especially when they can benefit from observing how they relate to others in the moment.

name: Prolonged Exposure (PE)
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is PTSD in adults.

name: Psychoanalysis
bestUsedFor: Most defensible for selected chronic, complex, and personality-level presentations where the person can use an intensive psychodynamic frame and where briefer therapies have been insufficient or are unlikely to address the depth of the pathology.

name: Psychodynamic Psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best supported across common mental disorders, especially depression, some anxiety and panic presentations, somatoform / functional-symptom presentations, substance-related disorders, eating disorders, and personality disorders.

name: Psychoeducation
bestUsedFor: Broadly useful across most psychiatric disorders.

name: Psychoeducation for Psychosis
bestUsedFor: Broadly useful across first-episode psychosis, established schizophrenia-spectrum illness, relapse prevention, discharge planning, rehabilitation, and self-management work.

name: Psychoeducational recovery groups
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is in severe mental illness, especially schizophrenia-spectrum and other long-term psychiatric disorders where self-management and recovery functioning are central.

name: Psychosis-specific self-management programmes
bestUsedFor: Best as part of continuing care for psychosis or schizophrenia, especially in community, early psychosis, rehabilitation, and relapse-prevention settings.

name: Psychosocial case planning
bestUsedFor: Best in severe mental illness, rehabilitation, discharge planning, community psychiatry, complex psychosis, repeated admissions, and presentations where functioning, support needs, or service coordination are central.

name: Recovery groups
bestUsedFor: Best as an adjunctive intervention in longer-term psychiatric care, community recovery settings, step-down services, psychosocial rehabilitation, and chronic illness pathways where personal recovery, self-management, and community participation matter.

name: Recovery planning for addiction
bestUsedFor: Best in alcohol and other drug treatment, dual-diagnosis care, inpatient discharge planning, residential rehab step-down, opioid agonist treatment support, relapse-prevention work, and recovery-oriented case management.

name: Recovery-oriented case management
bestUsedFor: Best in community psychiatry, rehabilitation, severe mental illness, complex psychosis, long-term support pathways, and step-down care where sustained psychosocial coordination is needed.

name: Recovery-Oriented Psychosocial Interventions
bestUsedFor: Best supported in rehabilitation for adults with complex psychosis.

name: Relapse Prevention Therapy for Substance Use Disorders
bestUsedFor: Best used after initial motivation has improved and the patient is actively trying to reduce, stop, or maintain abstinence, especially in alcohol use disorder and broader substance use disorders.

name: Relapse-Prevention Psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Strongest guideline-backed use is recurrent depression, especially after remission or partial remission in people at higher relapse risk.

name: Relational psychodynamic therapies
bestUsedFor: Best for complex depression, personality vulnerability, chronic relational problems, trauma-linked relational patterns, recurrent interpersonal crises, and presentations where symptoms are embedded in long-standing developmental and relational patterns.

name: Relational-cultural therapy
bestUsedFor: Best when the case formulation is strongly relational, especially in trauma-informed, women’s mental health, identity, marginalisation, or chronic relational-distress presentations.

name: Relationship-focused therapy
bestUsedFor: Best when relationship problems are contributing to symptoms or recovery.

name: Resource-linkage / coordination as therapeutic intervention
bestUsedFor: Best in severe mental illness, complex psychosis, recurrent admissions, step-down care, discharge planning, community psychiatry, and presentations where progress depends partly on support packages, service access, and continuity across sectors.

name: rTMS
bestUsedFor: Best-supported psychiatric use is major depressive disorder, particularly treatment-resistant or hard-to-treat depressive episodes.

name: Schema Therapy
bestUsedFor: Strongest and clearest use is personality disorder, especially borderline personality disorder (BPD) and other chronic personality pathology.

name: School-refusal CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for school refusal where anxiety/avoidance is central and the young person can work toward graded reattendance.

name: Seeking Safety
bestUsedFor: Best viewed as a stabilisation-oriented integrated treatment when the patient needs a present-focused approach, is not ready for trauma processing, or when a service cannot yet deliver trauma-focused integrated treatment.

name: Self-Management Interventions
bestUsedFor: Strongest formal guideline support is in psychosis and schizophrenia, where NICE recommends considering a manualised self-management programme as part of treatment and management.

name: Short-Term Psychodynamic Psychotherapy (STPP)
bestUsedFor: The strongest current evidence is in depressive disorders.

name: Short-Term Psychodynamic Psychotherapy for Depression (STPP)
bestUsedFor: Best used for adult depression when relational-emotional patterns and developmental difficulties in close relationships are central.

name: Skills-training groups
bestUsedFor: Best when there is a clear, observable skill deficit contributing to ongoing impairment.

name: Sleep Compression Therapy for Insomnia
bestUsedFor: Best used for chronic insomnia disorder when the clinician wants the core logic of sleep restriction but in a more tolerable, gradual format.

name: Social Cognition Training
bestUsedFor: Best used as a selective rehabilitation adjunct in psychosis or schizophrenia when social-cognitive deficits are clearly contributing to poor relationships, poor community functioning, or difficulty using rehabilitation opportunities.

name: Social Skills Training (SST)
bestUsedFor: Most defensible as a rehabilitation adjunct when there is clear behavioural social-skill deficit affecting recovery.

name: Social-anxiety-focused CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for social anxiety disorder in adults, and developmentally adapted CBT for children and young people.

name: Social-Communication / Parent-Mediated Autism Interventions
bestUsedFor: Best supported for children and young people with autism, especially preschool children where NICE says to consider parent, carer or teacher mediation, and for school-aged children where NICE says to consider peer mediation.

name: Social-role restoration work
bestUsedFor: Best in severe mental illness, rehabilitation, longer-term community care, step-down settings, and recovery pathways where the main challenge is not just symptom control but re-establishing a life structure and meaningful contribution.

name: Solution-focused brief therapy
bestUsedFor: Best as a brief pragmatic intervention for adjustment-type problems, mild to moderate distress, engagement work, or situations where a focused collaborative change conversation is clinically useful.

name: Specialist Supportive Clinical Management (SSCM)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for adults with anorexia nervosa.

name: Stabilisation-focused trauma preparation
bestUsedFor: Best as a preparatory phase for complex, unstable, unsafe, or high-risk trauma presentations where immediate trauma processing is clinically unsafe or unlikely to be tolerated.

name: STAIR (Skills Training in Affective and Interpersonal Regulation)
bestUsedFor: Best for complex trauma / complex PTSD-type presentations where the dominant problems are emotion regulation and interpersonal functioning.
aliases: Skills Training in Affective and Interpersonal Regulation

name: Strengths-based case management
bestUsedFor: Best in severe mental illness, especially where long-term community follow-up, rehabilitation, and recovery planning are needed.

name: Strengths-based practice
bestUsedFor: Best as a cross-cutting recovery-oriented approach in rehabilitation, community psychiatry, long-term care, and complex severe mental illness, especially when functional recovery, self-management, and meaningful life goals are central.

name: Structured clinical management
bestUsedFor: Best for BPD/personality disorder in public-sector or general mental health settings where a structured, consistent, manualised clinical model is needed and specialist therapies may not be available.

name: Support groups
bestUsedFor: Best as an adjunctive intervention for people or carers who benefit from shared experience, practical coping ideas, and community connection.

name: Supported digital CBT
bestUsedFor: Best as an initial or stepped-care treatment for mild to moderate common mental health problems, especially when access barriers, waiting lists, geography, mobility, or preference for remote care matter.

name: Supported digital trauma-focused CBT
bestUsedFor: Best as a selective access-expanding option for PTSD when the person is stable enough for trauma-focused work but barriers make face-to-face trauma therapy difficult or delayed.

name: Supported digital trauma-focused CBT (Self-Help & Digital Therapies)
bestUsedFor: Best as a selective option for PTSD or clinically significant post-traumatic stress symptoms when the patient is appropriate for trauma-focused work but remote or digital delivery is preferable or necessary.

name: Supported education
bestUsedFor: Best for early psychosis, complex psychosis rehabilitation, youth/young adult mental health, and severe mental illness where education is a meaningful recovery goal.

name: Supported Employment / Individual Placement and Support (IPS)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for psychosis / schizophrenia and complex psychosis rehabilitation when the person wants mainstream employment.

name: Supportive Psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: High-yield in ED, inpatient psychiatry, consultation-liaison psychiatry, older-adult psychiatry, severe comorbidity, adjustment reactions, and bridging phases before or between more specific therapies.

name: Supportive-Expressive / Psychodynamic Counselling Approaches for Depression
bestUsedFor: Most defensible for adult depression when recurrent relationship themes and difficult affects are central.

name: Systemic Family Therapy
bestUsedFor: Best used when a systemic formulation is clinically more useful than an individual-only one.

name: Task-centred practice
bestUsedFor: Best for circumscribed, practical, time-limited problems where rapid action is more useful than deeper exploratory work, such as housing, benefits, service engagement, daily-structure problems, adherence barriers, or role-function disruption.

name: Telehealth-delivered psychotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best when an evidence-based psychotherapy is indicated and telehealth is safe and clinically appropriate, especially for rural and remote patients, patients with travel barriers, and situations where continuity would otherwise be disrupted.

name: Telephone-delivered CBT
bestUsedFor: Best as a lower-intensity or access-expanding CBT format for mild to moderate common mental health presentations, especially where distance, mobility, wait times, or preference for phone-based care are major barriers.

name: Transference-Focused Psychotherapy (TFP)
bestUsedFor: Best supported for borderline personality disorder and closely related severe personality organisation.

name: Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (TF-CBT)
bestUsedFor: Strongest use is PTSD.

name: Trauma-Informed Skills Work
bestUsedFor: Most useful when trauma exposure has left the patient with major emotion-regulation or interpersonal difficulties, especially in complex trauma presentations.

name: Twelve-Step Facilitation (TSF)
bestUsedFor: The strongest evidence is for alcohol use disorder (AUD).

name: Values-based therapies
bestUsedFor: Best when a values-based mechanism is clearly central, especially in ACT-informed work for transdiagnostic distress, chronic health conditions, and problems maintained by avoidance and overcontrol.

name: Vocational Rehabilitation
bestUsedFor: Best used in rehabilitation for complex psychosis and other severe mental illness when the person’s recovery goals include work, study, or structured occupation.

name: Waitlist-bridging brief interventions
bestUsedFor: Best when waits are long and the patient has mild to moderate symptoms or is suitable for a low-intensity interim intervention.

name: Wake therapy / sleep-deprivation chronotherapy
bestUsedFor: Best as a specialist adjunctive intervention for selected depressive episodes where rapid mood improvement is clinically useful and the service can monitor the patient safely.

name: Workbook-based therapy
bestUsedFor: Best as guided self-help or low-intensity CBT for milder common mental health presentations, especially when a patient prefers written structure or when digital access is limited.

name: Worry-focused CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for GAD or transdiagnostic presentations where worry is the dominant maintaining process rather than panic attacks, compulsions, trauma re-experiencing, or social evaluative fear.

name: Written exposure therapy
bestUsedFor: Best as a brief trauma-focused PTSD treatment option when a concise, lower-burden exposure-based therapy is needed.

name: Youth IPT / IPT-A
bestUsedFor: Best-supported for adolescent depression, especially when interpersonal stressors are central.

name: Youth trauma-focused CBT
bestUsedFor: Best for children and adolescents with PTSD or clinically important PTSD symptoms.
